get.description:
Full alarm history (active + cleared) in descending time order —
unlike /active, this does NOT filter on Alarm.active, so cleared alarms
stay visible here instead of disappearing on clear.

Sorted by whichever happened more recently — raise or clear — via
COALESCE(cleared_at, timestamp), not just raise timestamp. A still-active
alarm (cleared_at IS NULL) sorts by its raise time same as before; a
cleared one jumps back to the top of the log at the moment it clears
instead of staying stuck at its (older) raise time, where a busy system's
stream of newer active alarms would otherwise crowd it out of view.

get.description:
Network-level topology for DMS/ADMS consumption.

Loads the published network SLD for the given client and returns:
  substations[]  — group_box nodes with from/to resolved via spatial containment,
                   each including the full DMS topology of the linked substation SLD
  connections[]  — line nodes with resolved from_group_box / to_group_box

Sl.24 — structured topology export for DMS/ADMS consumption.
Delegates to _build_substation_topology helper (shared with /topology/network).

Returns nodes[], branches[], and line_vertices[] by parsing the published
SLD topology JSON and joining against sld_components for stable UUIDs and
component_attribute_values for engineering parameters.

Resolves: Sl.15 (node list), Sl.16 (branch list), Sl.17 (switch position).

post.description:
Sl.15/16 — Sync sld_components from the saved topology JSON.

Called by the SLD editor after every successful topology save (when DMS
is enabled). Upserts one sld_components row per engineering node and
removes rows for nodes that no longer exist in the topology.

Skips purely graphical types (junction, measurement, custom_svg, etc.).
Idempotent — safe to call on every save.

get.description: Alias for /odar/indices — called by UI.

Outage report — paginated outage list + reliability indices for the date range.

The list is paginated (page/page_size) because outage volume can exceed any
reasonable single-page row cap; total/mttr/indices are computed over the FULL
matching range via aggregate queries, not just the page of rows returned, so
they stay accurate regardless of which page is being viewed.

get.description:
Regenerate the Fledge configuration CSV on demand from the durable DB
tables (device_feeders, point_mappings, alarm_limits), not the static
file an upload happens to write — that file only ever reflects whichever
device was uploaded most recently, so serving it directly silently drops
every other device's data once a second device is uploaded.

Pass device_id (matches the Devices tab's rtu_id, e.g. "RTUHVDC") to get
only that device's rows. No device_id returns every device.

base_value/deviation_value aren't persisted anywhere themselves (they're
only ever present in the transient upload CSV) — reconstructed here from
alarm_limits, which IS one of the 4 durable tables an upload writes:
base_value = high, deviation_value = high - low. Either missing, or a
negative (high - low), falls back to 0.

post.description:
Wipe all configuration data:
  - TRUNCATE device_substations, device_feeders, point_mappings, alarm_limits
  - Delete CSV files from seed_data/ and config/
Telemetry data (telemetry_points, telemetry_history) is NOT touched.

post.description: Enable an RTU's IEC104 south service (Fledge has no per-device toggle of its own).

Restart an RTU's Fledge/comms-gw container — e.g. a simulator whose
IEC104 south plugin has gotten stuck outputting stale/constant values.

Add an IEC104 north service to this RTU — Fledge additionally exposes
its south-ingested data as an IEC104 server so a remote master/LDC can
pull it. Mirrors this instance's own south exchanged_data (same
CA/IOA/typeid, since it's the same dataset). First call for a given RTU
recreates its container to publish the north port to the host (a brief
south disconnect/reconnect, same as the existing Restart Fledge button);
later re-adds after a remove reuse the already-allocated port.

delete.description:
Remove this RTU's north service entirely (deletes the Fledge service,
not just disables it) and clears north_port so the Admin portal reverts
to "+ Add North" — a disabled-but-still-configured north and a fully
removed one must look different in the UI, since only the former can be
re-enabled without recreating anything. The container's published port
mapping itself is left in place (harmless — nothing listens on it once
removed); it'll be transparently reused, not re-published, if north is
added again later (see add_north_port_and_restart).

get.description: Return all IEC 61850 relays linked to a hierarchy node. Returns [] if none.

Get all substations under a client node.

Returns all hierarchy nodes of 'substation' type, enriched with
device_substations data when available. Works for both RTU-based
systems (device_substations entry exists) and IEC 61850-only systems
(relay linked directly to hierarchy node, no device_substations entry).
When both an RTU and relay share the same hierarchy node, the RTU
device_substations entry takes precedence — no duplication.

Return every client hierarchy node together with all substations linked
under it. Substations are linked when a hierarchy node whose parent_id
equals the client node id either has a device_substations row (RTU-based)
or has a relay whose hierarchy_id points to it (IEC 61850-only, no RTU) —
same fallback pattern as get_client_substations() above.

"substation_id" is always the hierarchy node's own id (a real UUID) —
it is NOT device_substations.rtu_id. rtu_id is returned as its own field
for callers that specifically need the RTU string. This keeps the id
stable and consistent whether the substation is RTU-linked or
relay-only, since a relay-only substation has no device_substations row
(and therefore no rtu_id) to derive an identifier from.

post.description:
Bulk upload the register-map CSV — same shared site-wide template used
for RTU/MQTT (config/modbus_register_map_template.csv); only the Modbus-
relevant columns need filling in (see REGISTER_MAP_REQUIRED_CSV_COLUMNS).
Upsert by (slave_id, point_name) — one device can have many slaves, so
the same point_name can legitimately repeat across different slaves.
Re-uploading updates existing rows and adds new ones, never deletes rows
missing from the file (same convention as ICD re-import — see
feedback_icd_import_is_upsert).

Column mapping from the shared template:
  parameter            → point_name
  modbus_register_add  → address
  slave_name, slave_id → as-is (required — grouping key, see ModbusRegisterMap)
  unit                  → as-is
  data_type             → normalized via _DATA_TYPE_ALIASES (template
                           uses generic names like "float"/"integer",
                           not the bool|int16|uint16|int32|uint32|float32
                           enum ModbusRegisterMap actually stores —
                           saving the raw string broke the admin UI's
                           data-type dropdown, confirmed live 2026-08-07)
  register_type         → read from an optional "register_type" column
                           if present and valid; the base template
                           doesn't carry this column at all, so when
                           it's absent (or invalid) this falls back to
                           inferring "coil" when data_type == "bool"
                           else "holding_register" (the common case for
                           MFM/energy meters) — override manually via
                           the edit form, or add a register_type column
                           to the CSV and re-upload, if a device
                           actually uses input_register/discrete_input.

scale defaults to 1/division_factor when division_factor is present and
non-zero (converts the RTU pipeline's divisor convention to ModbusC's
multiplier convention), else 1.0. offset defaults to 0.0 (no equivalent
column in this template).

get.description:
Public endpoint — lets the UI show a license invalid/expired banner
without authenticating first (the license gate itself blocks auth calls).

Includes the raw licensed-feature ceiling (`features`) so the Town Profile
admin UI can disable toggles for features the license doesn't grant,
instead of guessing from an unrelated town-tier label. `None` means no
ceiling applies (enforcement disabled) — the UI should treat that as
fully permissive, matching feature_flags.apply_license_ceiling's own
semantics for the same value.

Public endpoint — returns feature flags for the given client (or global profile).
No auth required so the frontend can gate nav items for all users.
